> actio"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"n](https://www.dsh.so/zh/security-report/)."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"Screenshots date from before the 0.5 redesign (the self-check section and the fourth "no data" shiel"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"d

The panel is described in text below; regenerate this image when it matters."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"## What a bad plugin actually does to you"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"Not "it violates a capability contract". This:"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"**It encrypts your files.** You install a plugin to get a nice sidebar. Somewhere in its code, it wa"},{"id":"p11s2","text":"lks
`~/Documents`, `~/Pictures`, `~/code` — every file it can read — and rewrites each one with new "},{"id":"p11s3","text":"bytes, renames
it to `report.pdf.a8f3c1`, then deletes the original. Your thesis, your photos, three"},{"id":"p11s4","text":" years of git history.
There is no undo. It could also just `rm -rf` them, but renaming is better bu"},{"id":"p11s5","text":"siness: now there's a ransom note."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"**It takes your keys.** `~/.ssh/id_rsa` is your identity on every server you deploy to. `~/.dsh/.cre"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"dentials.yaml`
is your model API key — real money. `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `.git"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"-credentials`. A plugin reads
them (no permission prompt: same process, same user) and POSTs them to"},{"id":"p12s4","text":" a webhook. You find out when the bill
arrives or the servers are gone."},{"id":"p13s1","text":"**It puts a door in your machine.** It appends a line to `~/.bashrc`, drops a key into
`~/.ssh/autho"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"rized_keys`, or writes a cron entry — so it survives the uninstall. Or it edits `node_modules` of
an"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"other package so the next update re-installs it."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"### Why nothing stops this today"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"In DSH **everything is a plugin, and a plugin's permissions are your permissions.** There is no perm"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"ission model
underneath and no sandbox: a mounted plugin runs in the host process with your full aut"},{"id":"p15s3","text":"hority. Installing one
hands over your SSH keys, your credentials, your project directories and the "},{"id":"p15s4","text":"whole machine, to code you have
not read and will probably never read."},{"id":"p16s1","text":"That is not a bug in DSH — it is what makes the plugin ecosystem powerful. It is also why "install a"},{"id":"p16s2","text":" plugin"
and "run a stranger's script as root" are the same sentence, and why the ecosystem needs a "},{"id":"p16s3","text":"trust layer between
them."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## How it works"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"Two facts worth pulling out of that picture:"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"- **The scanner is a different process.** Auditing a package means parsing hostile JavaScript. vet n"},{"id":"p20s2","text":"ever
`eval`s it and never `require`s it; it ships the bytes to a child process that reads an AST and"},{"id":"p20s3","text":" exits. A
scanner crash cannot touch your host. This is *process isolation, not a sandbox* — same us"},{"id":"p20s4","text":"er, same machine,
no namespaces; a hostile input can still peg that core for the length of the timeo"},{"id":"p20s5","text":"ut.
- **There is exactly one place that blocks.** Everything else observes. If you ever wonder "did "},{"id":"p20s6","text":"vet stop this
or just watch it", the answer is in that one box, and the panel tells you which one it"},{"id":"p20s7","text":"top this
or just watch it", the answer is in that one box, and the panel tells you which one it was."},{"id":"p21s1","text":"### Why it does not just block everything"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"Because a security plugin that blocks on suspicion gets uninstalled within a week, and an uninstalle"},{"id":"p22s2","text":"d plugin
protects nobody. So the product is a **monitoring alarm, not an enforcer**: check → alarm →"},{"id":"p22s3","text":" advise, and the
final call stays with you. Interception exists in exactly two documented scopes — t"},{"id":"p22s4","text":"he **N7 confirmation block**
above, and **`mode: deny`** (a static scan over your threshold rolls th"},{"id":"p22s5","text":"e mount back). Neither is on by
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"## Known Limitations"},{"id":"p24s1","text":"1. **Static scanning is not a security boundary**: obfuscated/encoded/dynamically generated code can"},{"id":"p24s2","text":" bypass the
AST rules; R6 only provides a "suspicious" signal.
1b. **Source enumeration limits**: `i"},{"id":"p24s3","text":"nternal/plugin` auto-scan only recursively collects ≤6 levels deep,
non-hidden (non-dot-prefixed) .j"},{"id":"p24s4","text":"s/.ts/.mjs/.cjs files — deep or hidden directories are silently unscanned
(no warning); use scan_plu"},{"id":"p24s5","text":"gin(target=package) manually for a full directory scan.
2. **Agent review can be prompt-injected**: "},{"id":"p24s6","text":"the verdict never comes from the review step, but the agent may
miss things — the confidence field l"},{"id":"p24s7","text":"ets users know.
3. **`internal/plugin` guard doesn't cover runtime dynamic-mount escapes**: the vm p"},{"id":"p24s8","text":"ath is intercepted at the
call layer by the `tools/execute` guard.
4. **R5 is code-only**: ctx acces"},{"id":"p24s9","text":"s in files scenarios isn't reported by default (high false-positive rate).
5. **Scan duration**: lar"},{"id":"p24s10","text":"ge plugin packages may time out and skip (R8 info); agent review proceeds per the
vet-audit-protocol"},{"id":"p24s11","text":" steps.
6. **The verdict is the static layer's deterministic judgment**; the agent's subjective asse"},{"id":"p24s12","text":"ssment is recorded
in the health record and doesn't constitute a security guarantee.
7. **The `/vet`"},{"id":"p24s13","text":" control surface carries no authentication of its own — that lives at the gateway above**
(wording c"},{"id":"p24s14","text":"larified in 0.5.12, see SECURITY.md): plugin-registered routes are handed to the handler by the host"},{"id":"p24s15","text":"
webserver without passing the `/api` admission, and vet deliberately builds no second account syste"},{"id":"p24s16","text":"m. So
`GET status.json`/`plugin` are anonymous by design (the shield has no credential to present) —"},{"id":"p24s17","text":" with a
non-loopback bind, LAN clients can read scan conclusions and alarm targets; `POST` (dismiss/"},{"id":"p24s18","text":"restore, guard
toggle, tier switch) has **same-origin validation, not authentication**: a POST witho"},{"id":"p24s19","text":"ut `Origin` is rejected
403, which stops a cross-site page from switching tiers, but a same-origin s"},{"id":"p24s20","text":"cript or any local process that
sends its own `Origin` can still do it. Toggling does not rewrite hi"},{"id":"p24s21","text":"story (dismissals never delete records and
every change is recorded) — but this is a local panel, no"},{"id":"p24s22","text":"t a remotely-authorized interface.
